title: Rafael and the Ghost
premise: Paloma Ishikawa, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of her family in row twelve of Flight 4471, receives calls on a burner phone from a voice she knows intimately: her husband Rafael, who died in that crash — or so the record says. The voice leads her to evidence that Flight 4471 was downed deliberately and that a powerful aviation consortium buried the truth, with Rafael alive as their coerced insider. As Paloma follows the phone's clues through falsified maintenance logs and silenced witnesses, she must decide whether to trade her one secret worth killing for — the black-box data proving the sabotage — to save Rafael's life before his handlers erase him. In the end she exposes the conspiracy at terrible cost, learning the voice was both truly Rafael and a weapon aimed at her, and she chooses justice outside the law over the duty that once defined her.
about_author: Marguerite Blackwood is a former air-safety analyst who left the industry after a case she was never allowed to close. She writes thrillers about grief, systems, and the people who fall between them.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Three years after losing her family on Flight 4471, Paloma works unwanted crash cases in a basement office, keeping her grief sealed behind procedure. A routine assignment forces her back into the 4471 file, where a page is missing. Emotional beat: controlled numbness cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: The Burner
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A padded envelope arrives containing a burner phone with no sender. At 3:07 a.m. it rings; the voice says her name the way only Rafael did. She demands proof; he recites a detail from row twelve no stranger could know. Emotional beat: vertigo — hope as a form of terror.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She runs the call recording against archived interviews and gets a 99.2% match to Rafael Ishikawa, deceased. Her colleague Dev notices her unraveling. She decides not to report the phone. Emotional beat: complicity begins; she crosses her first professional line.

chapters.title: What the Wreckage Said
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, present tense, disoriented. He wakes in a safehouse, remembering fire and then cold water, being told his death is the price of his family's safety. His handler, Voss, hands him the phone: make the calls, or the record changes again. Emotional beat: trapped love.

chapters.title: Maintenance Window
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Following Rafael's clue, she pulls maintenance logs for 4471's tail number and finds a repair signed off by a technician who died two weeks after the crash. The signature dates are impossible. Emotional beat: the first hard evidence — grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed Twice
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev traces the dead technician to a subcontractor owned by Meridian Aviation Group, whose executives sit on the very board investigating 4471. He confronts Paloma about what she's hiding. Emotional beat: loyalty strained by secrecy.

chapters.title: Instructions
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Voss escalates: Paloma has pulled the logs, and someone above Voss wants her handled. Rafael bargains for forty-eight hours to steer her away instead of toward them — while secretly encoding coordinates into his next call. Emotional beat: double agent within his own marriage.

chapters.title: Coordinates
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The phone rings with numbers disguised as a lullaby Rafael used to hum. They point to a storage unit in Newark. Inside: Rafael's real luggage tag from 4471, a hidden recorder, and half a black-box transcript. Emotional beat: proof he lived — and proof he knew he might die.

chapters.title: Tail Number
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She realizes she's being followed — a gray sedan, methodical, professional. She feeds it a false errand and meets Dev in secret, showing him everything. He warns her: whoever holds Rafael holds leverage over her. Emotional beat: fear metabolized into strategy.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. We meet the handler properly: a true believer protecting an aviation ecosystem he thinks too vital to scandalize. He reports upward that the widow is 'manageable,' knowing his superiors disagree. Emotional beat: banality of institutional evil.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A Meridian lawyer offers her a settlement, an apology, and closure — if she surrenders 'any recovered flight data.' She understands they know about the recorder. That night the phone rings: Rafael begs her to take the deal. Emotional beat: the cruelest possibility — that he's protecting her from himself.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She turns the tables, using the phone to interrogate Rafael about things only the man she loved would know — and one thing he gets wrong. Is he compromised, replaced, or testing her? Emotional beat: identity as the true crime scene.

chapters.title: Water Landing
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Flashback chapter: the crash itself. Rafael survives the ditching, is pulled from the water by Meridian's recovery team before rescuers arrive, and is shown footage of Paloma and their daughter to secure his obedience. Emotional beat: the origin wound revealed.

chapters.title: Half a Transcript
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev decodes the partial black-box transcript: a cockpit warning sequence consistent with deliberate sensor spoofing, plus a name redacted but rhythmically guessable — a Meridian VP. Dev is nearly run down leaving the archive. Emotional beat: knowledge becomes mortal danger.

chapters.title: The Second Phone
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma discovers a second burner sewn into Rafael's old jacket — his own, pre-crash, with messages he sent himself planning to blow the whistle. The voice on the other phone has been following a script built from these. Emotional beat: devastating ambiguity — puppet or partner?

chapters.title: Trade
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She contacts Voss directly and offers the deal: the recorder and transcript for Rafael, extracted alive, in person. Voss agrees too easily. She spends the night preparing contingencies with Dev, hiding the true original data. Emotional beat: cold clarity — she is now the investigator of her own trap.

chapters.title: Hangar Nine
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The exchange at a decommissioned hangar goes wrong on cue: Voss intends to take both data and widow. Rafael breaks script, turning on his handlers to shield Paloma. Gunfire, darkness, the gray sedan burning. Emotional beat: love choosing its side at last.

chapters.title: Flight Path
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. On the run with a wounded Rafael, she finally hears his full account — and forgives what can be forgiven. But the original recording reveals one more thing: the order to down 4471 came from inside the safety board itself. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into indictment.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Paloma refuses every legal channel — the law is the conspirator's instrument. Instead she routes the full evidence to the victims' families simultaneously, making suppression impossible. Meridian's stock collapses; arrests begin. Emotional beat: justice as detonation.

chapters.title: The Voice on the Line
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Voss, cornered, makes a final attempt on them both; Rafael takes the bullet meant for Paloma and survives barely, but the burner phone dies in his hand mid-call. Emotional beat: climax — the ghost becomes flesh by nearly becoming a ghost again.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Hearings, headlines, and the slow machinery of accountability. Paloma testifies not as a grieving wife but as the investigator who solved it. She resigns from the agency that failed her family twice. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt on her own terms.

chapters.title: After Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Paloma and Rafael's shared POV, alternating paragraphs. A year later, at the memorial wall, they stand together among names including their own daughter's. The phone rings once — a wrong number — and they let it go unanswered. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; love outlasting duty.
